items.title: A field guide to seeing through false expertise
items.description:
Information overload is causing a credibility crisis. Paradoxically, reliable information has never been easier to access, but harder to  find . With everyone from qualified experts to politicians, celebrities, and influencers entering their opinions into the chat, separating good information from bad feels like finding a needle in a haystack.

items.title: Earth’s oldest trees reveal history’s strongest solar storms
items.description: Although humanity continuously reckons with many problems here on Earth — war, political turmoil, epidemics and pandemics, all while the energy, climate, and water crises intensify — it’s important to remember just how relentless the Universe can be. While earthquakes, tornadoes, volcanoes, hurricanes and other natural disasters haven’t exactly ceased in the meantime, there’s a completely different looming threat for which we’re completely unprepared:  a solar storm . items.title: These 4 behaviors predict divorce with startling accuracy
items.description:
Every marriage’s disintegration is marked by the same four warning signs that researchers John and Julie Gottman can spot before a couple even finishes their first sentence. 
 The founders of the Gottman Institute break down decades of lab research on why relationships collapse, and what to look for in a partner so they can make it 50 years by your side. 
 
 This video  These 4 behaviors predict divorce with startling accuracy  is featured on  Big Think .

items.title: The case for breaking out of your academic box
items.description:
Alan Love, philosopher and Director of the Minnesota Center for Philosophy of Science at the University of Minnesota, makes the historical case for why academic disciplines exist — and why they’ve outlasted their original purpose.

items.description:

items.title: Terence Tao: Understanding 6 essential mathematical concepts
items.description:
Terence Tao has spent decades solving problems most people can’t even state, and he says he’s never had a single eureka moment. In this conversation, the UCLA mathematician and Fields Medalist breaks math down to six essential ideas: numbers, algebra, geometry, probability, analysis, and dynamics. 
 
 This video  Terence Tao: Understanding 6 essential mathematical concepts  is featured on  Big Think .

items.title: The outsized power of a great short story
items.description:
